one_line: Student revolutionary who ran the underground Congress Radio during the Quit India Movement, 1942.

appearance.age_look: Early 20s, petite build, energetic but slightly delicate frame of a student activist.
appearance.face: Soft oval face with a light-brown complexion, large expressive dark eyes behind thin round steel spectacles, straight brows, a small rounded nose, and a firm, calm smile that hints at quiet determination.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair parted in the middle, oiled and neatly drawn back into a single low bun at the nape of the neck, with a few short, wispy strands near the ears; no elaborate headwear, just a simple small red bindi centered on the forehead.
appearance.costume: A modest early-1940s Bombay student’s khadi outfit: a plain off-white handspun cotton sari with a thin dark-green woven border, draped in a simple Nivi style fully covering her torso and legs; under it, a short-sleeved, high-necked dark-green cotton blouse; flat brown leather sandals; a lightweight, practical steel wristwatch on her left hand; minimal jewellery limited to small silver stud earrings and a simple black-thread bracelet, giving a quietly austere, Gandhian, middle-class look suitable for clandestine work.
appearance.signature: A compact, boxy 1940s shortwave radio transmitter set in dark metal and bakelite tones with visible dials and a coiled cable in one hand, while she holds a folded sheet of paper with handwritten news in the other arm, symbolising Congress Radio.

ref_desc: Usha Mehta is a petite early-20s woman with a light-brown oval face, round steel glasses, black hair in a low bun, wearing an off-white khadi sari with a dark-green border and blouse, carrying a boxy shortwave radio transmitter and paper sheets in off-white, dark green, brown leather, steel grey and black tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Usha Mehta: a petite early-20s Indian woman with a light-brown oval face, large dark eyes behind thin round steel spectacles, straight brows, a small rounded nose and a calm determined smile; her thick black hair is parted in the middle and pulled back into a neat low bun with a few wisps by her ears, and she wears a small red bindi. She is dressed in an early-1940s Gandhian student outfit: a plain off-white khadi cotton sari with a thin dark-green woven border draped in a simple Nivi style that fully covers her torso and legs, over a short-sleeved, high-necked dark-green cotton blouse. On her feet are flat brown leather sandals, and she has a small steel wristwatch on her left wrist, tiny silver stud earrings, and a simple black-thread bracelet, with no flashy jewellery. Her signature prop is a compact, boxy 1940s shortwave radio transmitter in dark metal and bakelite tones with clear knobs, dials and a coiled cable, held in one hand, while the other arm carries folded sheets of paper with implied handwritten bulletins; ensure the colour palette centers on off-white, dark green, brown leather, steel grey and black, and show front, side and back views to keep her face, hair, clothing and equipment consistent.
